newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sees May car sales below forecast.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sees May car sales below forecast.

text.p: Chrysler Corp chief executive officer Robert Eaton said Thursday he expected U.S. car sales in May to be below the rate forecasted for the year.
But Eaton told reporters after the company's shareholder meeting that Chrysler still expects to see U.S. automotive sales of about 15.2 million units in 1997.
In April, industry-wide U.S. cars and light trucks were sold at a rate of about 14.6 million units, compared with a rate as high as 16.1 million units in January.
"I suspect from what I see, the market will be down again in May," he said.
Last year industry sales were 15.5 million units, marking an unprecedented third straight year of nearly flat sales.
Eaton declined to comment specifically on how much the nation's No. 3 automaker could recoup from production lost to a 29-day strike that ended last week over outsourcing at a Detroit engine plant.
But he felt the company had to accept the strike, despite the estimated cost of $450 million in after-tax earnings for the second quarter.
"We felt very strongly it was in the best interest of the company, its sharholders and all of its employees to outsource that production."
Eaton said average incentives had risen from the rate of $785 per vehicle the company was paying at the end of the first quarter amid intensifying competition.
But he said he was not concerned about an industrywide decline in sales of profitable minivans.
"It's still an absolutely excellent market for us, and one that we continue to dominate," he said.
Eaton expected the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by an additional quarter- or half-point this year, but he did not expect such an increase to affect the auto market.

He was pleased to see the recent strengthening of the yen, but said the weak yen would continue to boost Japanese automotive sales until the currency falls to its underlying "structural rate," which he estimated was between 100 and 105 yen to the dollar, compared with about 116 currently.
Eaton expected production of Crysler's new Plymouth Prowler retro-style roadster to go into production next week after a delay of several months due to a shortage of body panels.
The company planned to produce more than 1,500 of the vehicles in 1997 and about 5,000 in 1998 for sale at a suggested retail price of $39,000.

Eaton told shareholders at the annual meeting that Chrysler was halfway to its announced goal of buying back $2 billion in stock this year, on top of $3 billion in stock buybacks over the past two years.

In response to a question, Eaton defended the company's decision to withdraw from advertising on a much-hyped episode of the ABC television show "Ellen" last month in which the main character declares she is a lesbian.
"That particular episode because of the sensationalism that was out there with the media, we just felt was just not a good environment for us to present our products," he said.
He said the company had a policy of not discriminating on any basis including sexual orientation and notedit resumed its advertising on subsequent episodes of the show.
((-- Martin Wolk, Reuters Seattle bureau, 206-386-4848))
